Hi Jay / Marta,

Thanks — good questions. Short answer up front: transient KV-cache evictions are treated as automated runtime events and not documented as "exceptions" in the exception register; manual overrides to routing policies are considered operational exceptions and follow our exception workflow (record, approve, review).

Details below and I attached a short context doc (SIG_Control3_Context.pdf) and our SOC2 excerpt (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) for the sections that map to this control. If that doesn't cover what you need, happy to set a 30-minute call — I can do Wednesday afternoon PST.

1) Transient KV-cache evictions
- These occur frequently as part of memory pressure heuristics in the serving runtime. They are treated as routine runtime behavior, logged at debug/trace level, and used for metrics/alerts (latency spikes, cache miss rates). 
- They are not escalated to the exception register because they are deterministic and part of normal operation; we track them as operational metrics and correlate to incidents when they exceed thresholds.

2) Manual routing overrides / emergency fallbacks
- These are manual actions taken by on-call or Platform Ops to route traffic to a lower-cost/faster model variant or a different region to maintain availability.
- We treat those as exceptions: they must be recorded in the exception register within 24 hours, include the reason for the override, the approver, and a post-action review.
- Approvals: The on-call engineer can enact the override during a live incident, but post-hoc approval from the on-call manager (or SRE lead) is required for the register entry.

Evidence included: the PDF has the runbook excerpt and a screenshot of the exception register entry template. The SOC2 excerpt maps this practice to CC6.1/CC7.1.

If you'd like, Neha (Security) and Priyom (Platform Ops) are copied — they can join a call to go deeper on operational workflow.

Hi Marta / Jay — quick follow-up from the Platform/Security side. Short answer: we have a hybrid approach.

- Automated triggers: Certain classes of automated failover (region failover or autoscaler-driven capacity reductions) create an internal incident in our incident system (Jira Service Management) which is linked programmatically to the exception register metadata. That incident includes the initial detector (alert id), timeline, and automated remediation steps.

- Manual overrides (on-call): If an engineer manually performs a routing override, the platform emits an audit event (immutable log entry) and we require the engineer to create a ticket within 24 hours. We also have a lightweight UI in the ops console that surfaces a "Create exception ticket" button post-override to simplify this.

I've pasted the runbook excerpt below and attached the context PDF with screenshots. If helpful, we can record a short screen-share showing the console flow. Priyom can demo the UI if you want a walkthrough.

-- paste: runbook excerpt --
When performing manual routing overrides:
1) Execute override via Ops console (requires SSO + MFA).
2) Ops console writes an immutable audit event containing user, timestamp, and override parameters.
3) Engineer clicks "Create exception ticket" which pre-populates a Jira ticket with audit event metadata.
4) Post-incident, on-call manager reviews and approves the register entry; closure requires a short RCA if the override was part of an incident.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security, Product Compliance

Hi Jay / Marta — following our call on Friday (notes below), here is the written interpretation you can include with the SIG response. This is intentionally concise so your assessors can map it to SIG Q3 fields.

Written interpretation (for SIG Control 3):
Redwood Inference classifies runtime cache evictions (e.g., KV cache evictions) as normal operational behavior and not as exceptions requiring entry into the exception register, provided no customer-impacting SLA breach or security incident results. These events are logged at a high-fidelity level and are used in metrics/alerting and capacity planning.

Manual routing overrides and emergency fallbacks are classified as exceptions. The operator who performs the override must authenticate via SSO+MFA; the action generates an immutable audit event. The platform provides a UI affordance to create a linked incident/ticket pre-populated with audit metadata; if a ticket is not created automatically, the operator must create one within 24 hours. A post-action approval/review by the on-call manager or SRE lead is required and documented in the exception register.

If your assessors need a mapping table, we can provide the SOC2 control references and sample register entry. Attached: SIG_Control3_Context.pdf, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf.

Thanks for the review — please confirm if this is sufficient for your risk team or if you want a short appendix that maps to the exact SIG question IDs.
